learning.title: Verify the artifact that ships: committed blob, live body, read schema - never a stand-in
learning.trigger: Any scope claim, body-validation claim, or behavior claim made from something adjacent to the real artifact: a working tree that still holds uncommitted hunks from another PR, a local copy of a PR body, a validator from a stale branch, or a schema inferred from an action's name (night of 2026-11-17, four instances: 504's body validated against a stale validator; 512's reported caps-only scope shipped the format fix too - twice; mcp.discover read as 'the gateway namespace' from its name).
learning.rule: Every verification reads the artifact that ships, in the place it ships from: scope claims diff the COMMITTED blob ('git diff origin/main', never the worktree - uncommitted hunks from other work silently ride the push); PR-body claims validate the LIVE fetched body (gh pr view --json body) against the validator on main, re-fetched after gh pr edit; contract claims read the generated schema text, not the action name; CI claims read the check's own run list per branch, not the rollup. Adjacent artifacts (worktree, local copy, name, rollup) are how a wrong claim feels verified. Names are pointers, not artifacts: a worktree named for SHA A can sit at SHA B (2026-11-17, PM twice in one night - read a queue-state instead of the PR comment, then a worktree's cosmetic name instead of the verdict's Head: field); the verdict's Head: field and the checkout reflog are the record.

verification.requirement: A scope claim carries its mechanical check inline (e.g. 'git diff origin/main | grep -c <the-excluded-pattern> == 0'); a body claim carries the live validator output; a schema claim cites file:line of the read. If the check cannot name the artifact it ran against, the claim is unverified.
